# Graph layout

> [DreamShader](../index.md) » [Generation](index.md) » **Graph layout**

The pass that assigns editor coordinates and comment boxes to the nodes a compile just created.

| | |
| :-- | :-- |
| Runs on | `UMaterial` (including the hidden ThinCustom base) and `UMaterialFunction` |
| Runs after | the graph is built and the outputs are connected; before the material is recompiled |
| Source control | the optional [`Layout`](../language/layout.md) section and `#Region` / `#EndRegion` |
| Produces | node positions, `UMaterialExpressionComment` boxes, named reroutes (`DS_<variable>` under `Blocks`, `DS_Shared_*` under `Classic`) |

Which pass that is, is the project's [Graph Layout Style](#layout-styles). `Blocks`, the default, and the
two other styles computed on the compiler's IR are described under that heading. **When layout runs**,
**Explicit layout** and the sections after it describe `Classic`, the 1.x pass, which works on the
finished graph and which a project can still choose.

## When layout runs

*`Classic` only.* A style computed on the IR has no such guard: it is laid out before a node exists, and
always runs.

| Condition | Behaviour |
| :-- | :-- |
| fewer than 2 expressions in the graph | skipped |
| **1200 or more** expressions, and no `Layout` section | skipped, with a log line |
| a `Layout` section is present | explicit path |
| otherwise | automatic path |

The large-graph bail-out logs:

```text
Skipping automatic layout for large DreamShader graph ({Count} nodes). Existing generated positions
will be used.
```

The threshold is on the expression count of the finished graph, not on source length. It is checked
only on the automatic path — an explicit `Layout` section is always honoured, at any node count.

> [!NOTE]
> **Layout always runs, since `2.0.0`.** It used to be skippable: the graph you saw in the
> [preview](../tools/preview.md) or on a not-yet-materialized material was **unlaid out** — nodes sat
> in the tall single column the construction pass leaves them in — and layout only appeared once the
> asset was materialized, cooked or generated by the commandlet. A *Lay Out In-Memory Graphs* project
> setting was added to turn it back on, defaulting on; `2.0.0` removes the setting and the skip with
> it. The only remaining opt-out is the large-graph guard above. See
> [Ephemeral materials](ephemeral.md) and [Project settings](../settings/project.md).
>
> *(since 2.0.0)* The pass reports one slow-task frame per node on every compile. Through 1.x an
> interactive compile ran it *quiet*, one frame per block; the 2.0 emitter does not use that mode.

## Layout styles

*(since 2.0.0)* **Project Settings ▸ DreamShader ▸ Graph Layout Style** chooses what lays a generated
graph out. `Blocks` is the default. A graph takes the chosen style the next time its source is rebuilt;
node positions are not part of the [divergence digest](divergence.md), so an asset built under another
style never reads as hand-edited.

| Style | Reads | In short |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `Blocks` *(default)* | the compiler's IR | a page of boxes in source order, one per `#pragma region` or run of statements; no wire leaves a box — see below |
| `Classic` | the finished engine graph | the 1.x layout: blocks recovered from the material's outputs, `DS_Shared_*` named reroutes between them |
| `SourceBands` | the compiler's IR | one horizontal band per statement of the source, top to bottom in the order of the text; inside a band, a tidy tree that grows leftward from the statement's value |
| `Layered` | the compiler's IR | the whole graph in layers by distance from the outputs (Sugiyama): crossings reduced by barycentre ordering, rows aligned on the median of their neighbours |

### Blocks

The graph the way a person lays one out by hand: a box per step, the boxes in reading order, and a named
reroute wherever a value goes from one box to another.

- **A box is a region, or a run of statements.** Consecutive statements of one innermost `#pragma region`
  (a 1.x `Region`) are one box, titled with the region's name; statements outside every region are cut
  into runs of at most forty nodes, titled after the first and last variable they define. A region that
  holds other regions is a box around their boxes, so nested boxes never overlap. A function's outputs
  are a box of their own, to the right of the page.
- **Inside a box** the nodes are one small layered drawing, left to right.
- **No wire leaves a box.** A value another box reads gets a named reroute declaration beside it —
  `DS_<variable>`, or `DS_Shared_<n>` for a value no variable names — and one usage in every box that
  reads it. A constant is not rerouted: it is written again where it is read. What drives the material,
  or a function output, leaves its box through the `DS_<output>` pair that stands in front of every output
  in any style; the usages stand in a column beside the material's node.
- **The page** packs the boxes like words in a paragraph — left to right, then the next line — in source
  order, to a page about 1.8 times wider than tall.

The reroutes and the repeated constants are nodes of the generated graph, as the `DS_Shared_*` reroutes of
`Classic` are: the decompiler looks through them, and so does the [graph parity comparator](../contributing/testing.md).

### What the IR styles share

- **Columns are distances.** A node's column is its longest path to a root — the material's outputs, a
  function's outputs, a statement node; in `Blocks`, to whatever nothing else in its box reads — so every
  wire runs left to right and never backwards.
- **`#pragma layout` is obeyed to the unit.** A `Node` hint moves the named value's node to the given
  position and carries the nodes that hang off it; a `Comment` hint is passed through as the box it
  describes.
- **`#pragma region` is a box around its nodes**, nested regions inside their parents, each with a ring
  of padding so that titles do not collide.
- **`SourceBands` and `Layered` insert no reroute.** A wire that spans six columns or more is a *long
  edge*: it is counted in the `dump-layout` JSON and left as a wire. `Blocks` is the style that reroutes.
- **Nodes the IR does not know about are stacked beside their owner**: an IR node can become several
  engine expressions (a parameter with its mask, a sample with its coordinates), and the extra ones are
  placed in a column to the left of the one the IR value lives on.
- **Deterministic.** The same IR gives the same coordinates, on any machine; everything snaps to a
  16-unit grid.

Look before choosing — this draws every IR style for a source, builds nothing, and takes a second:

```powershell
./dsc.ps1 dump-layout DShader/Materials/M_Foo.dss        # …/Saved/DreamShader/Layout/**.svg, one per product and style
./dsc.ps1 dump-layout -All -Style Blocks -Json
```

Sizes in the picture are estimated from the IR (a node's pins and title); on a real compile the
engine's own node sizes are used, so spacing differs slightly and arrangement does not.

## Explicit layout

A `Layout` section pins named variables and declares comment boxes. Full grammar, argument tables and
parse diagnostics are on the [Layout](../language/layout.md) page; this section covers what the
placement pass does with them.

```c
Layout = {
    Comment(Name="Sampling", X=-1200, Y=-200, W=900, H=400);
    Node(Var="UV", X=-1100, Y=-120);
}
```

The explicit path is taken when the `Layout` block matched at least one `Node(Var=…)` against a
generated variable, **or** declared at least one `Comment(…)`. Then, in order:

1. **Pinned nodes.** Each `Node(Var=…)` writes its expression's editor X/Y exactly, and the graph
   node's position when one exists. A `Var` that names no generated variable is ignored silently.
2. **Comment boxes.** Each `Comment(…)` creates a `UMaterialExpressionComment` at the literal X/Y
   with the given W/H. An empty or whitespace-only `Name` is skipped.
3. **Unpinned nodes** are placed by iterative propagation from their already-positioned neighbours.
4. **Reroutes** are inserted for *distant* connections that cross a block boundary.
5. **The material root** is positioned near the outputs it consumes, then the output-feeding reroute
   usages are regrouped under a `Material Output` box.

### Comment box properties

| Property | Explicit `Comment(…)` | Automatic box |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Text | `DreamShader: ` + `Name` | `DreamShader: ` + block title |
| Position | literal `X`, `Y` | block bounds minus padding (110, 90) |
| Size | `max(120, W)` × `max(80, H)` | `max(420, width + 220)` × `max(240, height + 180)` |
| Colour | `Color=float4(…)` if given, otherwise `(0.10, 0.16, 0.22, 0.35)` | `(0.10, 0.16, 0.22, 0.35)` |
| Font size | 24 | 24 |
| Group mode | on | on |
| Comment bubble | visible in the details panel, coloured | visible in the details panel, coloured |

> [!WARNING]
> Every comment box DreamShader creates has its text prefixed with the literal `DreamShader: `, and
> that prefix is exactly what regeneration deletes. Writing `Comment(Name="Sampling", …)` produces a
> box reading `DreamShader: Sampling`; renaming it in the material editor to something without the
> prefix makes it survive the next rebuild — and a second box appears beside it. See
> [Regeneration](regeneration.md#what-survives).

### Placing the unpinned nodes

Propagation runs until nothing moves, capped at `max(32, pending count)` passes.

| Known neighbours | Position |
| :-- | :-- |
| both dependencies and consumers | the midpoint between them |
| consumers only | `consumerX - (nodeWidth + 140)`, same Y |
| dependencies only | `dependencyX + 360`, same Y |
| neither, ever | fallback column |

Collisions are resolved by bucketing positions into 80 × 80 slots; the *n*-th occupant of a slot is
offset vertically by `±((n + 1) / 2) * (nodeHeight + 40)`, alternating sign — the node's own
[estimated height](#node-footprints), so two nodes in one slot clear each other whatever they are.

Anything still unplaced goes into a fallback column at `bounds.MinX - 480` (or `-1200` when nothing
was positioned), starting at `bounds.MaxY + 240` (or `-620`) and stepping Y by each node's height
plus 40.

## Automatic layout

With no `Layout` section, the pass partitions the graph into **blocks**, lays each block out
independently, and stacks the blocks downward.

### Block construction

Blocks are built in this order and then stable-sorted by sort key, ascending.

| Order | Block | Title | Sort key |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 1 | one per distinct `#Region` name | the region name | region order |
| 2 | *(material)* one per **connected** material property input | `Output: <PropertyName>` | the material-property enum index |
| 3 | *(material function)* one per `UMaterialExpressionFunctionOutput` | `Output: <OutputName>`, or `Output: FunctionOutput` when unnamed | `1000 + declaration order` |
| 4 | every expression with no consumers that is not already a sink | `Generated Outputs` | `100000` |
| 5 | *(only if nothing above produced a block)* everything | `Graph` | `0` |
| 6 | expressions used by more than one block that no block owns | `Shared Inputs` | `-1000`, inserted first |

An expression appearing in exactly one block is assigned to it immediately. Ambiguous ones are
resolved over at most 16 passes by "which block already owns the most of my direct consumers";
leftovers take their first candidate. Every `NamedRerouteDeclaration` is finally forced into its
source's block.

### Cross-block reroutes

Any input that crosses a block boundary is rewired through a shared named reroute.

| Node | Name | Position |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `UMaterialExpressionNamedRerouteDeclaration` | `DS_Shared_<n>`, `n` counting from 0 | `source.X + 360`, `source.Y` |
| `UMaterialExpressionNamedRerouteUsage` | one per (declaration, consumer block) pair | `consumer.X - 360`, fanned out vertically by `±((slot + 1) / 2) * 80` |

Input channel masks are preserved across the rewire. On the automatic path every crossing connection
is bridged; on the explicit path only **distant** ones are, where distant means `|ΔX| ≥ 900` or
`|ΔY| ≥ 540`. The explicit path additionally bails out before inserting anything unless it built at
least two blocks and assigned owners to at least two expressions.

### Node footprints

Every step below works in real node sizes rather than a flat footprint. There is no widget to
measure at generation time — the commandlet has no editor UI, and even in the editor the graph's
node widgets do not exist yet — so the size is *estimated* from what `SGraphNodeMaterialBase`
assembles.

| Term | Contribution |
| :-- | :-- |
| Title bar | `46`, plus `20` per extra caption line from `GetCaption` |
| Pin rows | `28 × max(inputCount, outputCount)` |
| Expression preview | `124` when `UMaterialExpression::ShouldShowPreview()` — i.e. `!bHidePreviewWindow && !bCollapsed` |
| Body padding | `22` |
| Width | `max(48 + captionChars × 10, 56 + (inputNameChars + outputNameChars) × 8)`, clamped to `[140, 520]` |

Output pin names count toward the width only when `bShowOutputNameOnPin` is set. The estimate
deliberately errs high: over-estimating only loosens the graph, while under-estimating overlaps
nodes. Measurements are memoised for the duration of one layout pass.

This is what keeps a `TextureSample` — a node the preview thumbnail makes roughly twice the height
of a `Constant` — from being stacked on top of its neighbour, and what makes the comment boxes big
enough to actually contain what they are drawn around.

### Placement inside a block

A layered, Sugiyama-style layout.

1. **Rank** each expression by its longest path to a consumer: sinks are rank 0, and
   `rank(e) = max(rank(consumer) + 1)`. A cycle resolves to rank 0.
2. **Lane** every edge that spans more than one rank. An edge from rank `r` to rank `r + n` gets
   `n - 1` dummy slots, one per column it crosses, chained between its endpoints. Without them
   step 3 is blind to long edges — it only ever compares neighbours one rank apart — which is what
   let a graph read as a ball of wire even though each column was individually tidy. A lane
   reserves `34` of vertical room, so the wire gets a corridor rather than crossing whatever
   happens to be in the way.
3. **Reduce crossings**: 6 passes, each sweeping toward the outputs ordering every column by the
   average position of its consumers, then back toward the inputs ordering by its dependencies.
   Lanes take part on equal terms with real nodes. Barycentres are computed for a whole column
   before it is sorted, so the ordering cannot depend on how the sort pairs elements up; ties break
   on creation order.
4. **Stack** each column by real heights with a `60` gutter, centred on the block's mid-line.
5. **Straighten**: 4 passes, alternating direction. Each pulls every slot toward the average centre
   of its neighbours on the settled side, then repairs the column with an isotonic regression —
   the closest set of centres that still keeps the column's order and its minimum gaps. This is
   what turns a chain into a straight horizontal line instead of a staircase.
6. **Assign X**: a column is as wide as its widest node, and nodes are **right-aligned** within it,
   so a column's outputs line up and the wires into the next one stay short. Column `0`'s widest
   node has its left edge at `X = 900`; each further column sits `150` to the left of the previous
   column's left edge.

### Packing the blocks

Blocks used to stack in one column, which turned a material with several connected outputs into a
ribbon tens of thousands of units tall — readable only fully zoomed out. They are now laid out
around their own origins first, then packed into columns.

| | |
| :-- | :-- |
| Column height budget | `max(2400, sqrt(totalBlockArea / 1.6))` |
| Next block in a column | previous block's `bounds.MaxY + 420` |
| Next column | previous column's widest block `+ 520` |
| First block | `Y = -620` |

A block is wrapped to a new column when adding it would overrun the budget, unless the column is
empty — a block taller than the whole budget gets a column to itself rather than being split. With
few enough blocks to fit one column the result is the old top-to-bottom stack.

Comment boxes are drawn only after packing: a box placed before the move would be left behind by
the nodes it is supposed to contain.

### The material root

Two passes touch the root node, in order:

1. `RootX = combinedBounds.MaxX + 520`, `RootY = (MinY + MaxY) / 2 - 240`. The material graph's root
   node position is written too.
2. Output-feeding named-reroute **usages** are then pulled out of their computation blocks and
   stacked in a single column at `bodyBounds.MaxX + 420`, spaced by the tallest usage node's height
   `+ 40` (never less than 130); the root moves a further `widestUsage + 360` to the right; and the
   whole group gets its own comment box titled `Material Output`. The root is centred on the column
   by its own `420` height rather than a fixed 240.

Removing those usages from the computation blocks first is what keeps the per-property boxes tight.

## Layout constants

| Constant | Value | Applies to |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Output column X | `900` | left edge of the widest rank-0 node, and `FunctionOutput` nodes |
| Column gutter | `150` | gap between two columns — the wire corridor |
| Row gutter | `60` | gap between two stacked nodes in a column |
| Lane height | `34` | vertical room one long edge reserves per column crossed |
| Block gap Y | `420` | gap between two blocks in the same column |
| Block gap X | `520` | gap between two block columns |
| First block top | `-620` | Y of the first block |
| Column height budget | `max(2400, sqrt(area / 1.6))` | block packing |
| Node footprint | estimated per node, `[140, 520]` wide | bounds and spacing |
| Fallback footprint | `320 × 150` | measuring a null expression |
| Root footprint | `320 × 420` | the material result node |
| Comment padding | `110` X, `90` Y | automatic boxes |
| Minimum automatic box | `420 × 240` | automatic boxes |
| Minimum explicit box | `120 × 80` | `Comment(…)` |
| Reroute offset | `360` | declaration right of source, usage left of consumer |
| Reroute fan-out | `±((slot + 1) / 2) * 80` | stacked usages |
| Root gap | `520` | root right of the graph bounds |
| Output-usage column | `bodyBounds.MaxX + 420`, spacing `max(130, tallest + 40)`, root `+ widest + 360` | the `Material Output` group |
| Distant threshold | `|ΔX| ≥ 900` or `|ΔY| ≥ 540` | explicit path reroutes only |
| Crossing-reduction passes | `6` | per block |
| Straightening passes | `4` | per block |
| Owner-assignment passes | `≤ 16` | ambiguous expressions |
| Propagation passes | `max(32, pending)` | explicit path, unpinned nodes |
| Large-graph threshold | `1200` | automatic-layout bail-out |

> [!NOTE]
> These constants are not part of the stable surface. The generated-asset layout may change in any
> release; nothing in a `.dsm` depends on them except through a `Layout` section, which pins absolute
> coordinates and is unaffected.

## `Output:` block titles

The material-property block titles come from a fixed table. Every name below produces
`Output: <name>`; anything not listed produces `Output: MaterialProperty<enum index>`.

`BaseColor`, `MaterialAttributes`, `EmissiveColor`, `Opacity`, `OpacityMask`, `Metallic`,
`Specular`, `Roughness`, `Normal`, `AmbientOcclusion`, `Refraction`, `WorldPositionOffset`,
`PixelDepthOffset`, `SubsurfaceColor`, `CustomData0`, `CustomData1`, `DiffuseColor`,
`SpecularColor`, `SurfaceThickness`, `Displacement`, `CustomizedUV0`, `CustomizedUV1`,
`CustomizedUV2`, `CustomizedUV3`, `CustomizedUV4`, `CustomizedUV5`, `CustomizedUV6`,
`CustomizedUV7`, `Anisotropy`, `Tangent`.

A custom engine build that defines `MOON_ENGINE` adds five more:
`MoonEncodedAttribute0` … `MoonEncodedAttribute4` (the pre-rename `MooaEncodedAttribute…` spelling is an
accepted alias). Stock UE 5.3 – 5.8 does not.

## Construction-time positions

These are the coordinates nodes carry when layout is skipped — a graph of fewer than two nodes, or
1200 or more nodes with no `Layout` section, under `Classic`. Note the shape: X is fixed and Y just
steps down per node, so a skipped graph is one tall column with wires across it, not a bad layout.

| Node | X | First Y | Y step |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| every node the emitter creates, in the order it creates them | `0` | `-120` | `+180` |

*(since 2.0.0)* The 1.x table of per-kind positions — the whole-surface `Custom` node, the
`MakeMaterialAttributes` seed, property nodes, `FunctionInput` / `FunctionOutput` — went with the 1.x
generator: the emitter places every node it creates the same way, and the layout pass rewrites them.

Every `Outputs` binding also creates a named-reroute pair at construction time: the declaration at
`source.X + 420`, `source.Y`, and the usage at `X = 720`, `Y = -120 + max(routeIndex, 0) * 180`. The
declaration is named `DS_<sanitized route name>`, plus `_<index>` when the route is indexed;
a blank route name falls back to `DS_Output`.

## Notes

- `#Region "Name"` / `#EndRegion` in a `Graph` block do not move anything by themselves — they name
  blocks for the automatic path, and boxes for the IR styles. Regions nest; a `#Region` without a
  name is [`DSH2216`](../diagnostics/DSH2xxx.md#dsh2216), and an unbalanced pair
  [`DSH2217`](../diagnostics/DSH2xxx.md#dsh2217) / [`DSH2218`](../diagnostics/DSH2xxx.md#dsh2218).
  Grammar is on the [Layout](../language/layout.md) page.
- A `Layout` section with only `Node(Var=…)` entries that match nothing, and no `Comment(…)`, does
  **not** engage the explicit path — the automatic path runs instead.
- A second `Layout` section in the same block replaces the first entirely, with the warning
  [`DSH2258`](../diagnostics/DSH2xxx.md#dsh2258) *(since 2.0.0)*.
- Layout positions are not preserved across regeneration. A `Layout` section is the only way to make
  a node's position stable. See [Regeneration](regeneration.md).
- The [decompiler](../tools/decompiler.md) emits a `Layout` section in exactly the parse format, so a
  hand-arranged material can be exported and re-imported with its arrangement intact. This is
  controlled by the **Export Decompiled Layout** project setting, default on.
- Automatic layout reports a slow task titled `Laying out DreamShader material graph...`, with one
  frame per node reading `Positioning node {N} of {Total}...`.

## Example

```c
Shader(Name="Docs/M_Layout")
{
    Properties {
        vec3  Tint      = vec3(1.0, 0.4, 0.1);
        float Intensity = 2.0;
    }
    Settings { Domain = "UI"; ShadingModel = "Unlit"; }
    Outputs  {
        vec3  Color;
        float Alpha;
        Base.EmissiveColor = Color;
        Base.Opacity       = Alpha;
    }
    Graph {
        #Region "Colour"
        Color = Tint * Intensity;
        #EndRegion
        #Region "Alpha"
        Alpha = Intensity * 0.5;
        #EndRegion
    }
}
```

Automatic layout produces:

```text
comment  DreamShader: Shared Inputs        sort key   -1000
comment  DreamShader: Colour               sort key   region order
comment  DreamShader: Alpha                sort key   region order
comment  DreamShader: Output: EmissiveColor
comment  DreamShader: Output: Opacity
comment  DreamShader: Material Output      root + the output reroute usages
reroute  DS_Shared_0                       Intensity, used by two blocks
```

Pinning one node instead:

```c
    Layout = {
        Comment(Name="Colour", X=-1200, Y=-200, W=900, H=400);
        Node(Var="Color", X=-600, Y=-120);
    }
```

```text
comment  DreamShader: Colour               at (-1200, -200), 900 x 400
node     Color                             at (-600, -120), exactly
                                           every other node propagated from its neighbours
```
